title: Derived tensor over R with a complex of A-modules
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a map of commutative rings and let $N$ be a complex of $A$-modules. Regard each commutative ring as a sheaf of rings on the one-point site, so that complexes of modules, K-flat complexes and K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex] (which exist [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]), total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and the derived categories $D(R)$, $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] apply; a total complex $\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes_R N)$ with $E$ a complex of $R$-modules is a complex of $A$-modules through $N$. (1) If $\alpha:E\to E'$ is a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes of $R$-modules, then $\operatorname{Tot}(\alpha\otimes 1_N)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. (2) There is an exact functor of triangulated categories $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N:D(R)\to D(A)$, the left derived functor of $E\mapsto\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes_R N)$, which is everywhere defined and computed by K-flat complexes: for every K-flat resolution $F\to E$ the canonical map $E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N\to\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R N)$ is an isomorphism in $D(A)$, and for two K-flat resolutions of $E$ the resulting isomorphism between the two total complexes in $D(A)$ is canonical (compatible with composition for a third resolution). (3) A morphism $u:N\to N'$ of complexes of $A$-modules induces a natural transformation $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N\to-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N'$, represented for K-flat $F$ by $\operatorname{Tot}(1_F\otimes u)$ and compatible with composition of morphisms $u$; if $u$ is a quasi-isomorphism, then $\operatorname{Tot}(1_F\otimes u)$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every K-flat $F$ and the transformation is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply lem-pc-mixed-tensor-kflat-quasi-iso for first-variable inversion and second-variable inversion on K-flat complexes.

For each fixed N, obtain the left-derived universal pair, exactness and K-flat computation from lem-pc-mixed-tensor-pointwise-left-derived. Choose these universal pairs, which are determined up to canonical isomorphism.

Assemble the pairs using Mathlib leftDerivedNatTrans. Its identity, composition and comparison equations give a functor T and the required representative equation. For a K-flat resolution s:F → E, use the inverse of T(Qs) composed with epsilon_F; cancellation gives uniqueness. Cancellation of e2 with its inverse proves the cocycle equation.

Every derived object has a K-flat model from the existing functorial flat resolution. For a quasi-isomorphism u in the second variable, the comparison equation on that model has the two counits and Q_A(B(1,u)) invertible. Cancel the target counit to make the component of T(u) invertible. Naturality transports this to every derived object, hence T(u) is an isomorphism.
